chain.title: [Portal] Facebook connect UI + tenant self-unpublish
chain.what_this_session: (a) Portal Connections: a FacebookConnect component next to WordPressConnect. The tenant pastes page_id and a Page Access Token. It shows status and last_verified_at/last_verify_error, and a Test button calls the existing GET/POST /v1/integrations/facebook and /facebook/test. Record in the implementation notes that the backend takes a pasted token, not OAuth. (b) Unpublish must actually remove the post. Today DELETE /v1/publish-log/{id} only sets publish_log.status='unpublished', and the post stays live on the channel. Add delete_post(external_id) to WordPressAdapter (DELETE /wp-json/wp/v2/posts/{id}, which moves the post to trash) and to FacebookAdapter (Graph DELETE /{post_id}). Call it from the unpublish route before flipping the row, using publish_log.external_id. On a remote failure, return a clear error and leave the row as published. Then wire an Unpublish action with a confirm step into My Content / the publish log. (c) Disconnect with DELETE /v1/integrations/{wordpress|facebook}: delete the shared.tenant_integrations row and overwrite the secret with an empty tombstone via PutSecretValue. Do not call DeleteSecret, because the ECS task role has no DeleteSecret on acp/cms/* or acp/social/*. Audit the action and use acquire_scoped_conn so it survives AA-817 RLS. (d) Delete portal/page.tsx.bak.old and the stale 'static mockup' comment in WordPressConnect.tsx.
chain.why_now: The backend is mostly there, and this closes the T11 self-serve loop ('Cheap, now' in the S236 design review). Facebook pieces already appear in the pending list, but tenants cannot connect Facebook. Without the remote delete, a portal Unpublish button would tell tenants a post is gone while it is still public, a trust and AUP-adjacent problem.

The post is gone from the Page / WordPress (screenshot or curl of the post URL showing 404/trash), and publish_log moves from published to unpublished with unpublished_by='tenant:<id>'. Disconnect makes GET /v1/integrations/facebook return connected=false. Cross-lane review of the five S237 lanes (read-only). The lanes mostly fit together, but six things must be fixed before they run.

(1) AA-819 is planned twice, in cis-backend #3 and cis-portal #1. The two plans give different migration designs: 230 NOT NULL DEFAULT 20, versus a nullable override with a code default. Both lanes would also edit v1_publish.publish() and quality_gates.py. Pick one owner per part.

(2) The AA-817 migration 229 as written (ENABLE + FORCE + NULLIF policy on gold_aa_internal.tenant_tour_versions) would hide every row from aa_cis_admin, which owns the table. Migration 225's header and schema-ownership.md both say aa_cis_admin is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS. So the T2 worker, admin Content Quality, v1_tours on the main pool, AA-801/AA-793 jobs and portal AA-802 would all see 0 rows. 229 must follow the 115/116/145 pattern (ENABLE, no FORCE) or add an explicit admin policy. (4) TripPlanner slice 6b assumes a "228 top-k function", which the CIS 228 scope does not include.

(5) AA-818, AA-811, AA-679 and AA-712 each appear in two lanes, with overlapping Infra/IAM work that needs one owner.

(6) Two ordering rules clash and need an agreed migration flow. The AA-807 byte-copy guard needs the owner repo's main merged first. But Booking's REQUIRED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS check, and any CIS code that reads a new column, fail if the code deploys before the apply.
